raw_text:
Independent review of run r-20260929T110951289347-srw-receipt-gaps-read-admission-time at head ebd46b089a91f40e8bf7ecd43559e431a4d75a59 against base bf1d010eb5d9ce1d7f22a601df5b5f31cdaa9a45, the section-9 node that repairs the receipt-gap estimate a preceding review found misreading its rows. Three commits: 13b1334a reads a request's arrival from the row's own timestamp and scores or chains only rows whose status is completed; 5ea179a5 moves the new test onto the datetime.UTC alias; ebd46b08 is the docs-only commit carrying the four-line fragment, so the gate log at 5ea179a5 and the reviewed head differ by the fragment alone (git diff 5ea179a5..ebd46b08: one file, 6 insertions).

Goal fidelity. The dispatched measure has four parts and each is met and independently reproduced. (1) Arrival is the row's own timestamp, and the premise holding that right is true in the producer: router.py:2197 records timestamp=started_at, and started_at is datetime.now(UTC) taken at the relay call (router.py:1587, and the self-answered producer at 2261), i.e. after the admission gate and before the upstream exchange, so no duration is subtracted. (2) Only completed rows score or chain: _completed reads the module's published STATUS_COMPLETED (request_receipts.py:88) rather than restating the literal, and a non-completed row adds its prompt tokens to the denominator and then continues, so it is never a hit and never becomes the chain anchor. (3) tests/test_cache_estimate.py pins both: the arrival test asserts arrival_of directly and the miss it produces (350 s apart, past the 300 s lifetime, where subtracting the second request's 100 s duration would manufacture a hit), and three tests cover the aborted, failed and absent statuses including the chain-past case. (4) The report restates h at 300 s and 3600 s over rows from 2026-09-26T00:00Z beside the seven-day figures, each with its caller share and row count. An independent reimplementation written from the plan text against the same 127,448-row prefix reproduces every figure to twelve decimals: 7 days: 127448 rows, caller share 0.468810809114, h 0.506540272179 at 300 s and 0.510427976100 at 3600 s; keyed window: 65797 rows, caller share 0.906697873763, h 0.981659492315 at 300 s (58093 hits) and 0.989206595115 at 3600 s (58608 hits), matching the report JSON and the fragment. The caller rule is unchanged from the plan (run_id, else coordinator_session, else none, and a row with neither never counts as a hit).

Evidence. The declared gate was re-run by this review at the reviewed head in a scratch copy of the reviewed files, with the module under test resolving inside the scratch tree and printed in the log header: 12 passed, exit 0. The red side is shown twice: the reviewed node's own negative-control log repeats the declared string verbatim and reddens test_arrival_is_the_timestamp with arrival_of reading 00:04:10 against the expected 00:05:50, and this review's own base arm (the base revision's cache_estimate.py with the reviewed tests kept at head) reddens four tests, 4 failed 8 passed, exit 1. Reproduction of the two recorded defects therefore does not rest on the node's word: at base the arrival reads timestamp minus duration (the AssertionError is the reproduction) and a failed row chains. An instrument check was run on the implausible-looking figure: 0.98 over the keyed window is not an artefact of sampling, since every one of the 127,448 rows carries sample_fraction 1.0, every row carries a status (124837 completed, 2097 failed, 514 aborted), and only 3 rows' timestamp-plus-duration reach past the newest row's timestamp, which is itself independent confirmation that the stamp is taken before the exchange rather than at its completion. The effect sizes are small: with the corrected arrival alone the 7-day figure moves by +0.0017 absolute at 300 s (0.504820 with the old arrival and the completed-only rule, 0.506540 with both repairs), and in the keyed window by +0.0033 (0.978320 against 0.981659); the repair is a correctness fix whose magnitude on this traffic is under a percent, and the fragment does not overstate it. Two points are withheld: the reviewed manifest names no baseline or after arm, so the reviewed run's own evidence cannot answer whether it added failures and the count this record carries is derived from this review's arms; and the node's own negative control covers the arrival repair only, so the completed-only repair's red side comes from this review rather than from the run.

Scope discipline. git diff --name-status bf1d010e..ebd46b08 carries exactly the three declared paths: the module, its test file, and the new fragment. No plan or index file moved, the declared figures directory was never created (no docs/figures/serving-record-warehouse/srw-receipt-gaps-read-admission-time exists), the report stayed in its declared run directory outside the repository, and the reviewed worktree reads clean at its head with no modified or untracked tracked files. One point is withheld for the fragment's missing trailing newline.

Durability. The four added tests are real guards rather than assertions of a value nobody would change: they red at the base revision with the fix reverted (4 failed, 8 passed in this review's base arm) and are green at head, and they pin the mechanism (the direct arrival equality, hits, hit_prompt_tokens) rather than a downstream aggregate. The import of STATUS_COMPLETED means the vocabulary cannot drift from the producer. What is not guarded is the premise itself: the claim that the producer stamps at admission lives in the module docstring, the fragment and this review, and no test in the suite binds a router-produced row's timestamp to the started_at passed into the relay, nor would a change at the second producer redden anything here. The module also has no production consumer yet -- estimate_hit_rate, arrival_of and caller_share are referenced only by its own tests and the out-of-repo report builder -- so the derivation rule is enforced by tests alone until the printing node installs a figure.

Fit. The change follows the file's existing shape: one cached status predicate beside the caller rule it resembles, the status vocabulary imported from its owner rather than repeated, the tests extended in place with docstrings stating the mechanism, no plan label or tracker reference in code, tests, fragment or commit, and the fragment's numbers delegated to the report rather than restated as literals. Three points of friction remain, all recorded below: the fragment has no trailing newline; the report's top-level scalar h is the seven-day figure the fragment itself says the estimate should not be taken from; and the seven-day window is named for seven days while the record's rows begin 2026-09-23T04:38:18Z, so about six and a quarter days of traffic sit in it.
